profiles.title: The Myrrh-Bearing Women at the Tomb
profiles.subject: Scriptural scenes

overview.text: The published iconographic article explains the women’s name through the ointments they brought to Christ’s tomb. It places their Orthodox commemoration on the second Sunday after Pascha. Their vessels identify the purpose of their visit: care for the body of Jesus.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of a modern published explanation; full prose reproduction rights have not been established.

blocks.text: The women approach carrying vessels. An angel in white points toward the empty tomb and burial cloths, announcing that Christ has risen. The article describes this image as a representation of the Gospel encounter, in contrast with the theological Descent into Hades composition.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening description; A short history of this iconic representation

blocks.text: The selected Vologda icon is dated by its source to the end of the fifteenth or beginning of the sixteenth century. Its subject is the women’s encounter at the tomb; other images called Myrrhbearers instead assemble the commemorated saints without narrating this scene.

sourceRefs.locator: File description and displayed historic reproduction

blocks.reason: Necessary English description of the selected historic artwork and its published object metadata; no new theological interpretation.

blocks.text: The article’s discussion of hymnography emphasizes the women’s grief, their encounter with the angel, and their commission to announce the Resurrection. The focus is the empty tomb’s good news, rather than the depiction of Christ emerging from it.
